records.answer: Never store vaccines in the freezer compartment of household-grade combination refrigerator/freezer units because they have cold spots and temperature fluctuations. Avoid placing or storing any items other than vaccines, diluents, and water bottles inside storage units. Never store food and beverages in the unit with vaccines. Frequent opening of the refrigerator door to retrieve food items can adversely affect the internal temperature of the unit and potentially damage the vaccines. Never use dormitory- or bar-style combined refrigerator/freezer units for vaccine storage. These units have a single exterior door and an evaporator plate/cooling coil, usually located in an icemaker/freezer compartment.

records.answer: While vials are not usually considered hazardous or pharmaceutical waste, an empty rotavirus dispensing tube or oral applicator is considered medical waste and should be disposed of in a medical waste container. Administration of vaccines necessarily results in waste (e.g., empty vials), and despite best efforts, sometimes unused vaccines must be disposed of. The management of solid waste emanating from the healthcare environment is subject to federal and state regulations for medical and non-medical waste860, 861.
